descriptors.definition: Lessees must present comprehensive qualitative and quantitative disclosures in a single note or separate section to give users a basis to assess the effects of leases. This includes information on right-of-use assets, maturity analyses of lease liabilities, and expenses related to short-term or low-value leases.
inclusion: Additions and carrying value of right-of-use assets
Depreciation and interest expense
Expenses for short-term and low-value leases
Summary of leasing activities and potential cash outflows
exclusion: Leases with terms of one month or less from certain expense disclosures
Non-lease components unless integrated into asset measurement
nearby_distinctions: Differentiated from lessor disclosures which focus heavily on net investment risks, whereas lessee disclosures focus on liability obligations and right-of-use asset utilization.

descriptors.concept_name: Income Tax Accounting and Lessor Classification Basics
descriptors.definition: Recognition of lease assets and liabilities by lessees impacts deferred tax asset and liability measurements and recoverability assessments. Lessors classify all leases at inception into either finance or operating leases based on the transfer of risks and rewards incidental to ownership.
inclusion: Deferred tax recognition and measurement
Assessment of deferred tax asset recoverability
Substance-over-form lease classification by lessors
exclusion: Direct lessee tax deductions computed outside the scope of lease capitalization rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between lessee tax timing differences caused by capitalized lease adjustments and initial lessor classification rules based on ownership risks.

descriptors.definition: Lessors evaluate lease agreements at inception to classify them as finance or operating leases according to the transfer of ownership risks and rewards. Indicators include transfer of title, purchase options, major economic life lease terms, and specialized asset nature.
inclusion: Leases transferring ownership by the end of the term
Leases with bargain purchase options
Leases covering the major part of an asset economic life
exclusion: Leases failing to meet risk and reward transfer thresholds which default to operating leases
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts finance leases which shift ownership risks to the lessee with operating leases where the lessor retains those primary asset risks.

descriptors.definition: Lease classification depends on economic substance rather than legal form at the time of inception. The transaction is categorized based on whether substantially all risks and rewards incidental to ownership are transferred to the lessee.
inclusion: Evaluation of transfer of ownership
Assessment of specialized asset utility
exclusion: Form-based legal classifications that ignore underlying cash flow and risk distribution
nearby_distinctions: Focuses purely on the foundational evaluation standard rather than subsequent measurement mechanics.

descriptors.definition: At commencement, a lessor recognizes assets held under a finance lease as a receivable equal to the net investment in the lease. Manufacturer or dealer lessors recognize selling profit or loss in accordance with general revenue policies for outright sales.
inclusion: Recognition of lease receivables discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease
Derecognition of the underlying asset carrying amount
Recognition of selling profit or loss for dealer lessors
exclusion: Inclusion of initial direct costs in net investment for manufacturer or dealer lessors
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates standard lessors who capitalize initial direct costs into the receivable from manufacturer lessors who expense them immediately.

descriptors.definition: Lessors recognize operating lease payments as income on a straight-line basis or another systematic basis that reflects the benefit pattern. Initial direct costs incurred by lessors are added to the carrying amount of the underlying asset and recognized as an expense over the lease term.
inclusion: Straight-line or systematic recognition of lease income
Capitalization and systematic amortization of initial direct costs
Depreciation and impairment testing of underlying assets
exclusion: Immediate recognition of selling profit upon entering an operating lease
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with finance lease accounting where the asset is derecognized and a net investment receivable is recorded instead.

descriptors.definition: A lease modification is a change in scope or consideration not part of the original terms. It is accounted for as a separate lease if scope increases due to additional underlying assets at standalone prices; otherwise, non-separate modifications are reassessed prospectively.
inclusion: Evaluation of scope and consideration changes
Separate lease accounting when criteria for added assets are fulfilled
Prospective reclassification assessment for non-separate modifications
exclusion: Retrospective adjustments for changes that were anticipated in the original contract terms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between modifications that expand distinct asset rights treated as separate contracts versus changes requiring a combined prospective reassessment.

descriptors.definition: Lessors present finance lease assets as receivables representing the net investment, while operating lease assets are presented according to their specific asset nature. Extensive quantitative and qualitative disclosures are required to communicate cash flow timing and uncertainties.
inclusion: Balance sheet presentation of net investment for finance leases
Asset nature-based presentation for operating leases
Tabular quantitative maturity breakdowns
exclusion: Omission of residual risk management descriptions in qualitative notes
nearby_distinctions: Compares lessor presentation rules under Ind AS 116 with older standards like AS 19 which lacked formal lease modification guidance.

descriptors.definition: Lessor disclosure requirements provide users with insights into the amount, timing, and uncertainty of cash flows from leasing activities. Entities must outline risk management strategies concerning residual values, buy-back agreements, and variable payments.
inclusion: Explanation of leasing activity nature
Risk management practices on retained asset rights
Quantitative breakdowns of finance income and selling profits
exclusion: Standard financial statement line items duplicated without explanatory notes
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on lessor-specific risk exposures like buy-back guarantees rather than lessee liability repayment schedules.

descriptors.definition: A sublease is a transaction where an underlying asset is re-leased by an intermediate lessor to a third party while the original head lease remains active. The intermediate lessor classifies the sublease with reference to the right-of-use asset arising from the head lease rather than the underlying asset.
inclusion: Classification using the head lease right-of-use asset
Operating lease classification if the head lease is a short-term lease
Dual role tracking where the entity acts as both lessee and lessor
exclusion: Using the economic life of the original physical underlying asset for sublease classification criteria
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts primary lease classification which evaluates the underlying physical asset against sublease classification which evaluates the head lease right-of-use asset.

descriptors.definition: An intermediate lessor maintains primary obligations under the head lease while entering a secondary lease agreement with an ultimate sub-lessee. The sublease classification is determined by evaluating terms against the right-of-use asset created by the head contract.
inclusion: Maintenance of head lease accounting obligations
Separate lessor accounting for the sublease agreement
exclusion: Release of primary liability by the intermediate lessor upon executing a sublease
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates the original lessor-lessee dynamic from the layered intermediate structure involving three separate contractual parties.

descriptors.definition: A sale and leaseback involves an asset transfer from a seller-lessee to a buyer-lessor followed by a leaseback of that same asset. Accounting treatment depends on whether the transfer satisfies performance obligations to transfer control under revenue standards.
inclusion: Application of control criteria to determine sale validity
Accounting for transfers as true sales combined with a lease
Treatment of failed sales as financing transactions
exclusion: Automatic off-balance sheet financing classification for lessees
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes valid sales where asset control transfers from failed sales where the transaction is accounted purely as a collateralized borrowing.
